items: The Bical is lighter in alcohol, so it goes first; the 14% Verdicchio would make it seem thin if tasted after.
blocks.title: Tasting order for a flight

blocks.text: The two whites are a perfect pair to compare: same high acidity, but 12% vs 14% alcohol and lees/MLF texture vs pure steel fruit. Taste them side by side and practise calling alcohol and body.
blocks.title: Blind-tasting contrast

rows: Anyone wanting a light, food-friendly red
lineup.sub: Two serious whites, a savoury rosé and a light red. The Verdicchio at $12 is the value pick.

wines.concl: Very good, possibly outstanding. High alcohol and Medium(+) body are balanced by high acidity; old-vine concentration gives intensity; almond bitterness and early development add complexity and length.
exam: Classico = the historic core zone. Superiore = lower yields and higher minimum alcohol.
Riserva is the DOCG step up: Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva DOCG.
Alcohol on the SAT has only three levels: Low (under 11%), Medium (11–13.9%), High (14%+).
factors: Site
A single vineyard in Contrada Palombare, on the western side of the Castelli di Jesi zone. It was Campanelli's first-ever label.
Climate
Moderate Mediterranean, cooled by Adriatic breezes and hillside elevation along the Esino river, so acidity holds even in a warm year like 2022.
Grape
Verdicchio: naturally high acid, green-tinged, with a signature bitter-almond finish. One of Italy's most age-worthy whites; develops honey and fennel with time.
Vines
Part of the vineyard dates to 1955. Old vines give lower yields and more concentration, which helps explain the weight and 14% alcohol.
Winemaking
Soft pressing, free-run juice fermented in temperature-controlled stainless steel. No oak flavour expected.
wines.flag: 14% on the label = High alcohol on the WSET L3 scale (Medium stops at 13.9%). The high acidity hides it, which is exactly the trap in a blind tasting.
wines.name: Campanelli Palombare 2022
wines.ready: Drink now, with potential for further ageing.
wines.say: Single-vineyard Verdicchio, part-planted in 1955: lemon and ripe peach, real weight, and that classic bitter-almond finish.
wines.sub: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC Classico Superiore · Marche, Italy

wines.concl: Very good to outstanding. High acidity survives full MLF and is framed by creamy lees texture; pronounced chalky-saline length; layered primary and secondary notes give complexity.
exam: Full MLF and the acid is still high: proof of how naturally acidic Bical and a maritime climate are.
Large barrels (500–600 L) give texture and slow oxygen with little oak flavour, unlike 225 L barriques.
Bairrada is Portugal's maritime region, best known for tannic, high-acid Baga reds. Filipa's father, Luís Pato, is its most famous Baga champion.
factors: Climate
Maritime. The nearby Atlantic brings cool nights, and the Cértima river adds foggy mornings. Keeps alcohol low (12%) and acidity high.
Soil
Jurassic clay-limestone over white marls, with good drainage. Source of the chalky, saline feel.
Grape
Bical: high acid, citrus and stone fruit, white flowers, waxy texture. Rot-prone in a wet climate, so careful farming matters.
Winemaking

Hand-picked, slow pneumatic pressing, light settling. Fermented in 500–600 L barrels with native yeasts and bacteria (full MLF). Ten months on fine lees, unstirred, then blended in steel a month before bottling.
Ageing
The producer says it will age beautifully for around ten years. The 2025 is very young.
wines.flag: Calcário means chalk, a nod to the limestone soils. The back label spells out the method: indigenous yeasts, full malolactic, 500–600 L oak barrels, and 10 months on fine lees without stirring (some retailers say bâtonnage; go with the label).
wines.name: Filipa Pato Nossa Calcário Bical 2025
wines.ready: Can drink now, but has potential for ageing (about a decade, per the producer).
wines.say: Portugal's answer to white Burgundy: chalky, creamy and saline at only 12% alcohol, and built to age ten years.

wines.concl: Very good. More fruit and body than a pale Provençal rosé, kept fresh by Aglianico's acidity; the savoury, salty finish adds interest.
exam: Rosé methods: direct pressing vs short maceration. Blending red and white is not permitted for EU still rosé.
Rosé colour terms on the SAT: pink, salmon, orange.
Campania: Aglianico → Taurasi DOCG; whites Fiano di Avellino and Greco di Tufo.
factors: Climate
Warm Mediterranean, moderated by constant sea breezes on steep terraces above the water. Limestone soils add a savoury, saline edge.
Grapes
Piedirosso (locally Per'e Palummo) brings soft, juicy red fruit. Aglianico brings acidity and a touch of grip; it's the grape behind Taurasi.
Winemaking
Brief skin contact for colour, then fermented and kept without oak to protect fresh red fruit.
Producer
Founded in 1980 in Furore. The terraced 'heroic viticulture' of the Amalfi Coast.
wines.flag: The Gran Furor Divina Costiera crest on the label is a historic brand from 1942 that Andrea Ferraioli bought when he founded the estate with Marisa Cuomo in Furore.
wines.name: Marisa Cuomo Costa d'Amalfi Rosato 2024
pair: Spaghetti with anchovies or colatura (Cetara's anchovy sauce)
wines.ready: Drink now. Not intended for ageing; best by next summer.

sat.app: Medium salmon (the bottle reads salmon-pink; confirm in the glass)

wines.say: Not a pale pool rosé: real cherry and pomegranate fruit, plus sea-salt freshness from the Amalfi cliffs.

wines.concl: Good to very good. Pure, bright and balanced with fine tannins; lighter and simpler than village-level Burgundy, which fits both the appellation and the vintage.
exam: Burgundy pyramid: Regional (Bourgogne, Hautes-Côtes) → Village → Premier Cru → Grand Cru.
Two Hautes-Côtes zones: de Nuits and de Beaune. Higher elevation = cooler = more acid, less body.
2024 is a textbook marginal-climate vintage: disease pressure, low yields, lighter wines.
factors: Site
The Hautes-Côtes are the higher, cooler hills west of the famous Côte de Beaune slope. More wind and later ripening mean lighter body and brighter acid.
Vintage

2024 was a very hard year: rain almost nonstop, early mildew that hit Pinot Noir hardest, and tiny yields. A dry, sunny August and September saved the harvest. Reds came out lighter, juicy and fresh, with fine, ripe tannins.
Grape
Pinot Noir: thin skins, so pale colour, high acid, low-to-medium tannin and red-fruit aromas.
Winemaking
Estate-grown and bottled; described by the family as fresh and youthful. Expect little new oak, in line with the vintage.
wines.flag: Not the Beaujolais Guérin. It's estate-grown Pinot Noir from Change, in the hills behind the Côte de Beaune. The board's "Bourgogne Rouge" undersells it a little: Hautes-Côtes de Beaune is its own regional appellation, a step up from plain Bourgogne.
wines.name: Famille Guérin Hautes-Côtes de Beaune 2024
wines.ready: Drink now. Could hold 2–4 years; not designed for long ageing.
wines.say: Real Burgundy from the hills above Beaune: pale, juicy red cherry and raspberry, bright acid, light enough for salmon.
wines.sub: Bourgogne Hautes-Côtes de Beaune AOC · Burgundy, France
